quotes.reference: 1962 January, “Talking of Trains: Track Re-arrangement at Colwich”, in Modern Railways, Shepperton, Surrey: Ian Allan Publishing, →ISSN, →OCLC, page 10:

senses.definition: To make a recess (noun senses 1 and 1.1) in (something).
Often preceded by in or into: to inset (something) into a recess or niche.
examples: That gargoyle recesses into the rest of architecture.
Recess the screw so it does not stick out.

senses.definition: To conceal, to hide.

quotes.text: Get near fat Mr. Dutton, and behind the screen of his prodigious elbow, you will be comfortably recessed from curious impertinents.
quotes.reference: 1808 (date written), [Maria] Edgeworth, “Manœuvring. Chapter XII.”, in Tales of Fashionable Life, volume III, London: […] [S. Hamilton] for J[oseph] Johnson, […], published 1809, →OCLC, page 292:

senses.definition: To temporarily suspend (a meeting, the proceedings of an official body, etc.).

quotes.text: When Congress is recessed, he makes himself acquainted with those free United States, of which he is the gifted son.
quotes.reference: 1842 December – 1844 July, Charles Dickens, “In which the Travellers Move Homeward, and Encounter Some Distinguished Characters upon the Way”, in The Life and Adventures of Martin Chuzzlewit, London: Chapman and Hall, […], published 1844, →OCLC, page 400:

senses.definition: To make a recess appointment in respect of (someone).

quotes.text: To the National Rifle Association's delight, the Senate has hobbled the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives by failing to confirm a director since 2006, but [Barack] Obama hasn't made a recess appointment. […] "The President's view of his own power is a constrained one," says White House counsel Kathryn Ruemmler. "Many of his nominees have languished, but he's only recessed the ones that were critical to keep agencies functioning."
quotes.reference: 2013 January 14, Michael Grunwald, “Cliff Dweller”, in Time, volume 181, number 1, New York, N.Y.: Time Inc., →ISSN, →OCLC, page 27, column 3:

senses.definition: Of a meeting, the proceedings of an official body, etc.: to adjourn, to take a break.
Of an official body: to suspend proceedings for a period of time.
examples: This court shall recess for its lunch break now.
